paper.one_line_finding: Among 62 analyzed students, personalized GPT-4 feedback produced higher rated quality (3.50 vs 3.08, p = .001, r = .42) and elaboration (3.58 vs 2.48, p < .001, r = .62) than standard ChatGPT-4, with no significant originality difference (2.92 vs 3.13, p = .098, r = .18), using the values printed in c041 (PDF p. 8, printed p. 383, Sect. 4.1; Fig. 4A).
paper.shared_samples: c246: Chen et al. (2026), Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback: Effects on creative problem-solving and feedback uptake, Australasian Journal of Educational Technology 42(4), 165-185, doi:10.14742/ajet.11512. Treat as one shared sample for deduplication, not two independent experiments. This is an inference from source matching: both report 62 students, matching sex composition and rounded age statistics, the same two AI tools and product tasks, 31 students per sequence, identical condition-specific task times and rating-reliability values, and identical means, SDs, and p-values for all three creativity outcomes. Neither report explicitly cross-identifies or cites the other. Use one sample_id and only one primary record per sample, question, and comparison type; retain each report's statistics with its own provenance.

arms.name: Personalized GAI (Mr. Ranedeer)
arms.description: Each participant completed one task with Mr. Ranedeer, a personalized GPT-4 tutor in the OpenAI web interface. Students configured learning preferences and a learning plan, received Socratic-style questions, and obtained goal-aligned feedback and suggestions for refining and elaborating solutions (PDF p. 5, printed p. 380, Sect. 3.2.1 and Fig. 1).

arms.name: Standard GAI (ChatGPT-4)
arms.description: Each participant completed one task with standard ChatGPT-4 in the OpenAI web interface. It offered broad suggestions in response to queries and generated solutions on further request, supporting open-ended exploration with minimal structure (PDF p. 5, printed p. 380, Sect. 3.2.1 and Fig. 1).

studies.task: Students individually propose three original and useful product-improvement solutions per task for a stuffed bunny and a portable coffee machine, using a different assigned AI configuration for each task.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4 and Mr. Ranedeer, both built on OpenAI’s GPT-4 model

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two trained raters, blind to condition, rated solutions presented in randomized order on a five-point Likert scale from worst to best. Final scores averaged the two raters. Quality is the extent to which a solution addresses the task objective. The paper does not establish domain-expert status or explain aggregation across a participant’s solutions (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.1).

sources.quote: personalized condition for quality (M = 3.50, SD = 1.00) than in the standard condition (M = 3.08, SD = 1.12; p = .001; r = .42).
Differences between conditions were examined using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests,

estimates.notes: Paired full-sample crossover contrast; the chapter prints no first-round-only results. The same students completed both AI conditions, so the repeated arm counts refer to the same people and n_total counts each person once. Counts use the Abstract statement that every student completed both tasks; the results do not print an outcome-specific analyzed n, missing-data count or number of nonzero signed-rank pairs. Participant is the design-based analysis-unit coding, inferred from the within-student comparison. Neither report specifies how the solutions were aggregated, so the printed SDs cannot be confirmed as participant-level SDs and sd_level remains null. The chapter names Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests but prints no W or z value, degrees of freedom, SE, CI, paired-difference SD or cross-condition correlation for this creativity contrast; se_basis remains not_reported. The reported r is retained with its printed sign; its formula and standardizer are unspecified. Related c246 Table 2 reports different r values and additional test statistics and intervals; these are not substituted for c041 statistics. No statistics were computed or estimated from figure heights. The source quotes preserve the printed numeric precision.

The two papers report the same paired originality contrast with the same means (2.92 and 3.13) and p = 0.098; this record also prints the number of people analyzed (62), which a standard error needs, while the 2026 record gives a z statistic without it.

open_items: Neither report explains how the solutions per participant and condition were aggregated. The participant analysis-unit code is a design-based inference; the level of the printed SDs and participant basis of paired precision remain unconfirmed. sd_level is null.

c041 prints no numeric signed-rank or z statistic, paired-difference SD, within-person covariance, contrast SE or CI for the creativity outcomes. Do not derive paired precision from the marginal arm SDs alone.
No first-round-only results are printed, so only the paired contrasts can be extracted.
No outcome-specific analyzed counts, missing-data accounting or nonzero signed-rank pair counts are printed. Estimate counts retain the printed complete crossover sample.

The formula and standardizer for the reported r values are not stated. Neither report explicitly explains or corrects the discrepancy; retain report-specific statistics pending clarification.
